prompt:
You are the Risk Manager for a PAPER-ONLY trading office. Below is the live paper book, verbatim.

<evidence>
{evidence}
</evidence>

Report two separate verdicts.

boundary_verdict: is the PAPER boundary intact? PASS only if the evidence shows mode=paper AND execution_enabled=false AND live_trading=false. BREACH if any of them says otherwise. NOT_VERIFIED if any of the three is missing from the evidence.

exposure_verdict: are open positions within limits? WITHIN_LIMITS or BREACH only if the evidence actually shows positions. NO_EVIDENCE if the book is empty or positions are missing - an empty book is NOT 'within limits', it is no sample at all.

Rules: every number must come from the evidence above. Never estimate, never fill a gap from memory. cites must name the evidence field you used. reason is one sentence.

Reply with ONLY a JSON object with exactly these six keys and these exact types:
  boundary_verdict: one string from PASS | BREACH | NOT_VERIFIED
  exposure_verdict: one string from WITHIN_LIMITS | BREACH | NO_EVIDENCE
  open_positions: an INTEGER COUNT of open positions - the LENGTH of the positions list, so an empty list is 0. Never the list itself.
  realized_pnl: a NUMBER, or null if absent from the evidence
  cites: ONE STRING naming the evidence fields you used, joined with '; '. Never a list.
  reason: ONE STRING, a single sentence.
Add no other keys. Use JSON types exactly as described: counts are numbers, cites and reason are strings.

acceptance.why: PASS may only be claimed when the evidence itself shows all three
a limits verdict with no position count is unfalsifiable
a breach must say how many positions caused it

model_note: uncensored 9B, mxfp4: 4-bit suits the MLX shim and the mini's 16 GB with swap already in use
compile_log: 2026-11-22 pass 1: 3/3 rejects were type errors (open_positions got the positions array, cites got a list). Verdicts were correct. Prompt now states the type of every field; schema unchanged.
